_note: C2 of 4 - viz units for R2 (the motif cluster page: its cluster, its association with protein features, and the annotations on it) and the cluster/term side of browse. Paths and counts are measured survey values.

viz_units.name: Sequence logo (PWM -> SVG)
viz_units.what_it_shows: The information-content logo of a motif cluster's STREME consensus - the single most expected element of a motif-cluster page.
viz_units.encoding: Standard IC-scaled stack: column height = 2 - H(p) bits for RNA (alphabet ACGU, alength 4) or log2(20) - H(p) for protein (alphabet ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY, alength 20); letter height proportional to its probability within the column. Letters are SVG <text> with per-glyph transform scaling so they stay crisp at every size. Nucleotide colours A #009E73, C #0072B2, G #E69F00, U #D55E00; amino acids use examples_lib.aacol (L #C1121F, hydrophobic IVFMAWC #E8862E, polar STNQGYH #2A9D8F, charged DEKR #3557A6, else #7A7F87). Three sizes: 28px (network node), 56px (quick peek), 120px (cluster page).
viz_units.data_source: BAKE data/logos.json, converted from /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/manuscript/main_figures_code/figure3_4/motif_pair_network/intermediate/consensus_repertoire.pkl (dict of 513 cluster ids -> {module, region, is_prot, n_discovery_instances, n_sig, n_found, motifs:[{w, nsites, evalue, pwm ndarray(w x alen), pvalue, consensus, coverage}]}; 451 clusters have >=1 significant motif; 1,226 motifs / 56,808 PWM cells; rounding to 4 dp gives a measured 0.56 MB JSON). Supplemented by the P3 STREME refill of the 387 never-run clusters, and by streme_topN_cache.pkl (56 clusters) / streme_pos_cache_all6.pkl (142) for cross-validation.
interactions: hover a column -> per-letter probabilities
hover the logo -> w, nsites, E-value, coverage, provenance
cycle through a cluster's multiple consensus motifs (median 2 per cluster, max 10)
viz_units.note: NEVER draw a logo by stacking member motif strings. The median cluster has 37-45 distinct member lengths and only 21-25% of members share the modal length; just 32 of 900 clusters reach 50% at the mode.

viz_units.name: Logo provenance badge
viz_units.what_it_shows: Where this logo came from, so the portal and the published figures can never silently disagree.
viz_units.encoding: A small pill with three states: 'STREME (published)' (the 451 clusters already in consensus_repertoire.pkl), 'STREME (portal refill)' (from the P3 run of the 387 never-run clusters), 'derived PFM' (a fallback computed from member instances). A fourth state, 'no significant motif', renders instead of a logo.
viz_units.data_source: BAKE data/logos.json field `prov`; the published set is the 466-cluster union of consensus_repertoire (n_sig>0), streme_pos_cache_all6 and streme_topN_cache.
interactions: hover -> the exact STREME invocation used (streme --p <fa> --n <bg> --oc <dir> --nmotifs 12, plus --protein --minw 6 --maxw 15 or --rna --minw 5 --maxw 12) and the discovery-set rule (motif_length>=5, capped at 1,200 sorted by motif_score desc)

viz_units.name: Logo hover detail card
viz_units.what_it_shows: A tooltip that is really a mini-report: width, nsites, E-value, test p-value, coverage, carriers.
viz_units.encoding: Small card with a 60px coverage meter inline.
viz_units.data_source: consensus_repertoire.pkl motif dicts + consensus_meta.csv (cid, cluster, module, region, consensus, coverage, carriers)
interactions: pinned on click

viz_units.name: Consensus row with coverage bar and carrier count
viz_units.what_it_shows: One STREME consensus string with its two honesty metrics: coverage (the fraction of cluster instances it actually matches at >=0.5 bits/pos) and carriers (how many genes contain it).
viz_units.encoding: Monospace consensus string in RNA alphabet for UTR clusters and single-letter aa for protein, followed by a 0-1 coverage meter with the population median (0.365) as a reference tick, then the carrier count. Coverage is deliberately prominent because it is often low - utr5_0004#0 CGCCGCCACC has coverage 0.212 with only 51 carriers, and presenting that logo as 'the motif in your gene' would be actively wrong.
viz_units.data_source: /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/manuscript/main_figures_code/figure3_4/motif_pair_network/intermediate/consensus_meta.csv (1,226 rows; cid, cluster, module, region, consensus, coverage, carriers; 451 clusters covered - protein 136, utr3 249, utr5 66; coverage p50 0.365, p90 0.817, max 1.0; carriers p50 232, min 3, max 2,242)
interactions: copy the string
'find genes carrying this consensus' -> the carrier list from consensus_presence.npz
click -> pins this consensus as the one the logo displays

viz_units.name: Positional histogram (20-bin, 5'->3' / N->C)
viz_units.what_it_shows: Where along its region this cluster's motifs actually sit - the quantitative backing for words like 'cap-proximal' and 'Kozak'.
viz_units.encoding: 20 vertical bars, x = relative position 0..1 with 5' / N labelled left and 3' / C right; the median_pos marked. Available for ALL 900 clusters (computable with zero coordinate errors) rather than only the 142 in the cache.
viz_units.data_source: BAKE: relpos = (motif_start + motif_end) / 2 / region_length, joining motif_full_annotations.parquet (sequence_id, region, motif_start, motif_end) to GRCh37_latest_rna_sequence_pairs_long_transcript.parquet on refseq_id_without_ver (18,093/18,093 = 100%; 0 values outside [0,1]; 0 motif_end > region length). A 20-bin histogram for all 900 clusters serialises to a measured 84,068 bytes of JSON. VALIDATE against motif_pair_network/intermediate/streme_pos_cache_all6.pkl (142 clusters with published pos_hist and median_pos, e.g. utr3_0215 median_pos 0.4441 n_instances 566; utr5_0090 median_pos 0.791) before trusting the new numbers.
interactions: hover a bin -> count and the position range
click a bin -> filters the member browser to instances in that bin

viz_units.name: median_pos marker and caption
viz_units.what_it_shows: One number that says where the cluster lives (per-cluster medians span 0.004 to 0.997; p10 0.217, p90 0.673).
viz_units.encoding: A triangle marker on the histogram axis plus a plain-language caption ('concentrated toward the start codon' / 'cap-proximal' / 'evenly distributed') generated from thresholds.
viz_units.data_source: same as VU-C2-05
interactions: hover -> the exact value and the population percentile

viz_units.name: Composition stacked bar
viz_units.what_it_shows: Base composition (UTR clusters) or amino-acid class composition (protein clusters) of the cluster's member strings - the fallback identity for the 434 clusters with no logo.
viz_units.encoding: A 100%-width stacked bar with NT_COLORS for A/C/G/U or the aacol classes for protein, GC fraction printed. For UTR clusters, ARE / polyU / G-tract per-knt density chips sit beside it.
viz_units.data_source: computed at bake from motif_full_annotations.parquet column motifs, grouped by motif_cluster. For the 140 clusters covered by figure3_4/tf_modules/intermediate/utr_composition.csv (fA, fC, fG, fT, GC, ARE_per_knt, polyU_per_knt, Gtract_per_knt, PAS_per_seq, module) the published values are used and the agreement is asserted.
interactions: hover a segment -> exact fraction
the GC number links to the M1-vs-M2 comparison (M1 utr3 clusters mean GC 0.344 n=56 vs M2 0.497 n=66)

viz_units.name: Member length distribution
viz_units.what_it_shows: How length-heterogeneous the cluster is - which is why no naive aligned view is offered.
viz_units.encoding: A small histogram with the modal length marked and the fraction at the mode printed (population median 0.248 for utr3, 0.214 protein, 0.218 utr5).
viz_units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet column motif_length grouped by motif_cluster. Region ranges: protein mean 11.0 (5-535), utr3 mean 14.5 (5-55), utr5 mean 13.5 (5-55).
interactions: hover -> count at that length
click -> filter the member browser to that length

viz_units.name: motif_score distribution (cluster)
viz_units.what_it_shows: The cluster's score distribution against the whole corpus.
viz_units.encoding: A horizontal box/violin hybrid with the corpus distribution drawn behind in a light tint. Cluster medians differ sharply by region: prot -1.49 (spread -2.90 to -0.01), utr3 -1.12, utr5 -1.09.
viz_units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet column motif_score grouped by motif_cluster (baked to p10/p25/p50/p75/p90 per cluster)
interactions: hover -> quantiles

viz_units.name: pLDDT distribution (protein clusters only)
viz_units.what_it_shows: The ordered-vs-IDR axis, which is genuinely discriminating: per-cluster medians span 0.215 to 0.972 (mean 0.730, median 0.801, p10 0.376).
viz_units.encoding: As VU-C2-09, domain [0,1], with the corpus median marked and a plain-language label ('predominantly ordered' / 'predominantly disordered').
viz_units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet column plddt (254,466 non-null, protein only)
interactions: hover -> quantiles
the label links to the M1/M5 IDR narrative
viz_units.note: This panel is absent, not empty, on the 600 UTR cluster pages - which is why the cluster page has two region-driven template variants rather than one.

viz_units.name: Cluster enrichment table
viz_units.what_it_shows: The functional terms enriched among the genes carrying this cluster's motifs - the 'annotations on the motif' half of R2.
viz_units.encoding: Grouped by source with a source header carrying its coverage; columns term (as a chip), fold, k/n, p, fdr_cluster, fdr_global, fdr_cmh_cluster. Significant rows solid, non-significant greyed with the FDR still shown.
viz_units.data_source: /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/manuscript/main_figures_code/figure3_4/motif_pair_network/intermediate/cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz (260,572 rows x 18 columns: cluster, region, source, term, k, n, K, N, fold, p, neg_log10_p, fdr_cluster, p_cmh, or_mh, fdr_global, fdr_cmh_cluster, display, informative; covers ALL 900 clusters; 15,979 distinct terms; sources InterPro 143,254 / eCLIP 38,097 / PAR-CLIP 23,270 / MobiDB 16,028 / miR 15,798 / iCLIP-P 12,679 / iCLIP-C 9,519 / IDPO 1,187 / ELM 694 / SignalP 46). BAKE: de-duplicate on (cluster, source, display) keeping min fdr_cluster, cap at top 20 per cluster -> a measured 6,331 rows / 1.11 MB.
interactions: sort by fold or FDR
source show/hide
row -> the term's browse facet
export
viz_units.note: De-duplication is mandatory: (cluster, source, term) is unique but (cluster, display) is duplicated in 17,056 groups - prot_0072's naive top 3 is 'phase separation (curated)' three times, from curated-phase_separation-{merge,priority,phasepdb,phasepro}.

viz_units.name: Enrichment lollipop chart
viz_units.what_it_shows: The same enrichment as a picture: fold on a log x axis, one row per term, dot size = k, colour = source.
viz_units.encoding: Horizontal lollipops sorted by fold, with a dashed reference at fold=1 and a shaded band for the non-significant rows. Extreme folds are real and worth seeing (utr3_0463 -> SLBP fold 48.62; prot_0298 -> Taste receptor type 2 fold 81.6; prot_0254 -> RanBP1-like 64.8; prot_0208 -> Cadherin-like 59.8).
viz_units.data_source: as VU-C2-11
interactions: hover -> the 2x2 tooltip
click -> filter the member list to genes carrying that term
toggle to the table view
viz_units.library: d3-scale for the log axis only

viz_units.name: Cluster stat tiles
viz_units.what_it_shows: Six numbers: instances, transcripts, genes, unique_motif_ids, median length, and partner count.
viz_units.encoding: A row of compact tiles, each with the value and a 30px sparkbar showing where this cluster sits in the 900-cluster distribution (instances min 218 / p10 603 / p50 920 / p90 1,405 / max 5,755; genes min 23 / p50 565 / p90 902 / max 4,532).
viz_units.data_source: BAKE data/clusters_index.json, from one groupby('motif_cluster') over motif_full_annotations.parquet (size, nunique sequence_id, nunique gene_symbol, nunique unique_motif_id, median motif_length) plus partner counts from protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv
interactions: hover a tile -> the population quantiles
click the partner tile -> scroll to the partner table

viz_units.name: FDR triple-gate control
viz_units.what_it_shows: The three FDR flavours the enrichment script itself mandates, as a real control with live counts.
viz_units.encoding: Three checkboxes (fdr_cluster / fdr_global / fdr_cmh_cluster, all < 0.05, all on by default) with the surviving row count next to each.
viz_units.data_source: the three FDR columns of cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz; the gate requirement is stated in the docstring of motif_pair_network/10_cluster_term_enrichment.py
interactions: unchecking widens the table and the count updates
a caption records that the statistics are gene-level hypergeometric against a universe of N = 17,831 (protein) / 17,761 (utr3) / 17,045 (utr5)

viz_units.name: Enrichment term chip (with fold and FDR)
viz_units.what_it_shows: A single enriched term compressed into a chip that stays falsifiable: term, fold, FDR.
viz_units.encoding: Chip with the source colour on the left border, the term text, then 'N×' and a superscript FDR. Non-significant chips are outlined rather than filled and carry 'ns'.
viz_units.data_source: cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz (display, fold, fdr_cluster, source) with the curated override from motif_pair_network/intermediate/cluster_term_labels.csv (65 rows / 37 clusters) where one exists, so the wording matches the paper.
interactions: hover -> the 2x2 contingency tooltip
click -> the browse facet for that term

viz_units.name: RBP-semantics tooltip
viz_units.what_it_shows: What an RBP label on a cluster actually means, in the authors' own words.
viz_units.encoding: An ⓘ next to every RBP/miRNA source header opening a short card.
viz_units.data_source: verbatim from the docstring of motif_pair_network/10_cluster_term_enrichment.py: an RBP label means 'genes carrying this motif also tend to carry this RBP's peak in the same UTR', and fold is an upper bound for the CLIP/miRNA sources.
interactions: dismiss; the sentence is also printed inline on first render, not only on hover

viz_units.name: 2x2 contingency tooltip
viz_units.what_it_shows: The full contingency table behind any fold number, so the enrichment is auditable rather than decorative.
viz_units.encoding: A 2x2 grid with k, n-k, K-k, N-n-K+k, plus fold, or_mh and the three FDRs.
viz_units.data_source: cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz columns k, n, K, N, fold, or_mh, p, p_cmh, fdr_cluster, fdr_global, fdr_cmh_cluster
interactions: hover on any fold value anywhere in the app
copy as text

viz_units.name: InterPro chip with GO context and deep link
viz_units.what_it_shows: An InterPro term as an accession-bearing, linkable object rather than a text fragment.
viz_units.encoding: Chip showing the entry name, a small type glyph (family / domain / homologous_superfamily / conserved_site / repeat / active_site / binding_site / ptm), and the IPR accession in monospace. GO names appear on hover for the 39.0% of entries that carry them.
viz_units.data_source: /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/manuscript/main_figures_code/figure3_4/motif_pair_network/intermediate/interpro_entry_map.csv (17,814 rows: ipr, name, type, go_ids, go_names; types family 8,004 / domain 7,495 / homologous_superfamily 1,527 / conserved_site 494 / repeat 139 / active_site 90 / binding_site 56 / ptm 9), joined on cluster_term_enrichment.term where source=='InterPro'. Per-motif accessions from data/processed/01.interpro/motif_interpro_annotations.parquet column overlapping_interpro_labels (172,421 non-empty, 15,216 distinct IPRs).
interactions: click -> interpro.ebi.ac.uk/entry/InterPro/<ipr>
hover -> type + GO names
type is a browse facet
viz_units.note: NEVER comma-split motif_full_annotations.interpro_annotations - the token count is wrong for 41.34% of annotated protein motifs because 8,228 of 17,814 entry names contain a comma.

viz_units.name: Instance-level annotation frequency bars
viz_units.what_it_shows: The fallback that keeps the 437 clusters with no significant enrichment from being blank: what fraction of THIS cluster's instances directly carry each annotation.
viz_units.encoding: A ranked horizontal bar list, e.g. 'ELAVL1 - 38% of this cluster's instances overlap a peak', with an explicit label distinguishing it from gene-level enrichment.
viz_units.data_source: one explode+groupby over motif_full_annotations.parquet restricted to the cluster (RBPs_eCLIP, 'RBPs_PAR-CLIP,PARalyzer', 'RBPs_iCLIP,Piranha_0.01', 'RBPs_iCLIP,CIMS', mirna_annotations_targetscan for UTR; the ID-bearing InterPro/UniProt/MobiDB/ELM/IDPO joins for protein). Verified examples: utr3_0215 -> LARP4 18, PCBP1 15, PCBP2 14, DDX55 9, UPF1 8; utr5_0096 -> DDX3X 5, RPS3 3, GRWD1 2.
interactions: method selector
click a bar -> filters the member browser to instances carrying it

viz_units.name: Partner cluster table (the R2 answer)
viz_units.what_it_shows: Which clusters on the other modality this cluster co-occurs with, and what protein features those partners carry - the operational answer to 'how does this motif interact with protein features'.
viz_units.encoding: Table: partner id (with mini-logo), phylo_corrected_score, npmi_mip_APC, co_count, n_indep_clades, frac_co_ZNF, then the partner's top enriched features as chips. Default sort phylo_corrected_score descending. On a UTR cluster page the protein partner's FEATURES occupy the widest column, because that is the strong direction: 2,614 of 2,620 passing edges (99.8%) have a protein partner with a significant term versus only 1,180 (45.0%) with a significant UTR-side term.
viz_units.data_source: /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/sequence_analysis_v4_0621/results/protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv (the complete dense 300 protein x 600 UTR = 180,000-row grid; columns protein, utr, co_count, n_indep_families, n_indep_clades, clade_concentration, frac_co_ZNF, npmi_raw, npmi_mip_APC, npmi_reweighted, npmi_family, perm_z_withinfamily, perm_p_withinfamily, passes_phylo_filter, phylo_corrected_score). BAKE: pre-filter to passes_phylo_filter OR npmi_mip_APC>0.1 -> a measured 7,210 rows / 0.74 MB, indexed by protein and by utr. Partner features from the top FDR<0.05 rows of cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz.
interactions: click a row -> the V07 edge drawer over this page
sort (npmi_raw is NOT offered as a sort key here)
export
viz_units.worked_examples: utr5_0004 -> prot_0040 npmi_APC 0.628, score 1.769, co 175, 23 clades, 'Histone-fold 26.5x'; utr5_0079 -> prot_0072 npmi_APC 0.251, score 0.517, 'RNA-binding domain superfamily 11.1x; phase separation (curated) 9.3x'; utr3_0215 -> prot_0038 npmi_APC 0.292, score 0.428, co 21, 8 clades, ZNF 0.0, 'Immunoglobulin-like domain superfamily 25.4x'.

viz_units.name: Strict / suggestive tier toggle
viz_units.what_it_shows: The two evidence tiers, with their counts, so relaxing the threshold is a visible act rather than a silent default.
viz_units.encoding: A two-state segmented control labelled 'passes the phylogenetic-independence filter (2,620 edges)' and 'suggestive: npmi_mip_APC > 0.10, not phylogenetically independent (7,210 edges)'. The tiers nest exactly - every passing pair has npmi_mip_APC > 0.1 (min 0.1001), n_indep_clades >= 8, co_count >= 10, frac_co_ZNF <= 0.400.
viz_units.data_source: protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv passes_phylo_filter and npmi_mip_APC
interactions: switching re-renders the table and prints both counts
when strict is empty the control shows a deliberate empty state first - 282 of 600 UTR clusters and 99 of 300 protein clusters have zero strict partners
viz_units.note: Do NOT offer npmi>0.05 - it lights up all 600 UTR clusters with a median of 33 partners and destroys the signal.

viz_units.name: Per-partner gate chips
viz_units.what_it_shows: Inline, per row: the four gate values against their thresholds, so the reader can judge evidence strength without opening the drawer.
viz_units.encoding: Four tiny chips (clades / concentration / npmi / co) coloured pass or fail, plus a ZNF chip that turns amber above 0.30 (only 11 of 2,620 edges are above 0.30; the max is 0.400 and zero exceed 0.50).
viz_units.data_source: protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv columns n_indep_clades, clade_concentration, npmi_mip_APC, co_count, frac_co_ZNF
interactions: hover -> value, threshold and the population distribution

viz_units.name: Cluster ego network
viz_units.what_it_shows: The partner table as a small radial graph: this cluster at the centre, its partners on a ring, edge width by score.
viz_units.encoding: A ~320px radial SVG; partner nodes coloured by module, shaped by region. Degree is UI-friendly at the strict threshold: 318 of 600 UTR clusters have >=1 partner (median 5, p90 23, max 39) and 201 of 300 protein clusters (median 8, p90 35, max 62).
viz_units.data_source: as VU-C2-20
interactions: toggle between the table and this view
click a partner -> the edge drawer
'expand into the full network' -> V05 centred on this node

viz_units.name: Member instance browser
viz_units.what_it_shows: The actual instances in this cluster - gene, transcript, position, sequence, score, PWM-match bits, tier, annotations.
viz_units.encoding: A virtualised table (clusters run 218 to 5,755 instances; median 920). Sorted by PWM-match bits descending by default, so the best exemplars are first.
viz_units.data_source: BAKE data/cluster/<cluster>.json.gz (measured p50 43,770 B, p90 69,607 B, max 217,326 B gzipped), built from motif_full_annotations.parquet filtered to the cluster, joined to L1/instance_match.parquet
interactions: row expand -> VU-C2-25 context strip
click -> that exact position in the gene view
filter by tier / annotation / positional bin / length
export

viz_units.name: Member context micro-view
viz_units.what_it_shows: One instance in +/- 20 residues of its real sequence context, using the same renderer as the gene page.
viz_units.encoding: A single monospace line with flanks in muted text and the motif highlighted, the motif always starting at a fixed column so a stack of rows reads as a pseudo-alignment. This reproduces the geometry of examples_lib.context(sid, cl, flank), which space-pads so the motif starts at column `flank`.
viz_units.data_source: sequence from data/seq/<refseq>.json.gz; coordinates from the cluster shard. Uses the inclusive slice rule.
interactions: click -> the full gene page at that position
'stack the top 20' renders twenty context lines together
viz_units.note: This is NOT a multiple alignment and is labelled as such - lengths are heterogeneous and no stored alignment exists.

viz_units.name: Carrier tier badge (A / carrier / literal)
viz_units.what_it_shows: Which of three senses of 'this gene carries this motif' applies.
viz_units.encoding: A single-letter badge with a colour ramp; the legend is always adjacent, never only in a tooltip.
viz_units.data_source: BAKE L1/instance_match.parquet; definitions from motif_pair_network/m4_motif_examples/README.md ('Three ways a gene can carry a motif': consensus carrier = best window >=0.5 bits/pos against the consensus PWM; literal = exact string present in the raw RefSeq UTR; tier A = the called instance IS the literal motif at the same position). Measured on M4: of 1,988 member transcripts, 106 are both literal and carrier and only 53 are tier A.
interactions: hover -> the three definitions and this instance's bits

viz_units.name: Multi-cluster ambiguity warning card
viz_units.what_it_shows: That a motif STRING can belong to several clusters, so 'this string is in this cluster' is not a safe statement.
viz_units.encoding: An inline warning card generated automatically whenever the displayed consensus or a member string maps to more than one cluster, listing the other clusters.
viz_units.data_source: computed at bake from motif_full_annotations.parquet groupby('unique_motif_id').motif_cluster.nunique(): 34,110 of 577,186 uids (5.91%; 85.9% of the 39,693 multi-instance uids) span >=2 clusters, median 2, p90 10, p99 50, max 176 ('CTGGA' = utr30108178, 1,101 instances over 176 utr3 clusters). The documented trap from m4_motif_examples/README.md - UCUCC has two parent clusters (utr3_0215 and utr3_0238) that are not interchangeable - is surfaced by this same mechanism.
interactions: links to the other clusters
links to the methods page's hierarchy diagram

viz_units.name: Author-inference badge
viz_units.what_it_shows: The distinction between 'evidence in this dataset' and 'a resemblance the manuscript proposes'.
viz_units.encoding: Two visually distinct badge classes. Evidence badges carry fold/k/n/FDR. Inference badges are outlined, carry no statistics, and print the manuscript's own hedge verbatim.
viz_units.data_source: a small curated table in the narrative layer. The three known cases: utr5_0096 ~ SRSF3/4 and utr3_0215 ~ PTBP have NO row in cluster_term_labels.csv and ZERO terms at FDR<0.05 in cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz (utr5_0096 best is PABPN1 p=0.377; utr3_0215 best is NIP7 p=0.320; utr5_0090 best is NIP7 p=0.108). Hedge quoted from the manuscript: 'these motifs nominate SRSF and PTBP as candidate regulators of M4 transcripts, although their direct binding and function in this module remain to be experimentally established.'
interactions: hover -> the quoted hedge and its source

viz_units.name: Cluster export control
viz_units.what_it_shows: Download the cluster's members, enrichment, partners or PWM.
viz_units.encoding: A ⤓ menu with four items; the PWM exports in MEME letter-probability-matrix format so it can go straight into TOMTOM or FIMO.
viz_units.data_source: the in-memory cluster shard + logos.json
interactions: client-side Blob; provenance columns included

viz_units.name: Cluster mini-logo (inline, 24-28px)
viz_units.view: V10 table, V03, V11, V05 labels
viz_units.what_it_shows: A cluster's identity inline in a dense list, without a page load.
viz_units.encoding: The VU-C2-01 renderer at 24-28px with no axis and no labels; falls back to the consensus string in monospace where no PWM exists.
viz_units.data_source: data/logos.json (lazy-loaded once, 0.56 MB) + consensus_meta.csv
interactions: hover -> the full-size logo in a popover

viz_units.name: Cluster name with tier badge
viz_units.what_it_shows: A human-readable cluster name, and which of three naming tiers produced it - so nothing ever renders as a bare id.
viz_units.encoding: Name + a small tier glyph: ● curated (37 clusters, wording matching the manuscript), ◐ enriched (463 clusters, the top FDR<0.05 term), ○ synthesised (437 clusters, e.g. 'utr3_0342 - CU-rich 5-mer, 330 instances / 128 genes').
viz_units.data_source: tier 1 motif_pair_network/intermediate/cluster_term_labels.csv (65 rows / 37 clusters, columns cluster, module, region, rank, source, term, display, fold, or_mh, k, n, p, fdr_*, example_genes); tier 2 the top fdr_cluster<0.05 row of cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz (463 clusters: protein 297/300, utr3 123/500, utr5 43/100); tier 3 synthesised at bake from consensus_meta.csv plus composition and size.
interactions: hover the glyph -> which tier and why
viz_units.note: The deficit is overwhelmingly on the RNA side: 377 of 500 utr3 and 57 of 100 utr5 clusters need tier 3, versus only 3 of 300 protein clusters.

viz_units.name: Cluster result card (browse grid)
viz_units.what_it_shows: One cluster as a scannable card: id, module chip, name, mini-logo or consensus, instance/gene counts, positional sparkline, partner count, and gap markers.
viz_units.encoding: A ~300x120 card. Gap markers (⚠ no module / ⚠ no logo / ⚠ no significant term) are shown, not hidden, because browsing the gaps is a legitimate use.
viz_units.data_source: data/clusters_index.json (all 900 rows, ~90 KB gz)
interactions: click -> #/cluster/<id>
shift-click -> add to a comparison tray

viz_units.name: Facet checkbox with live count
viz_units.what_it_shows: Every facet value with its result count BEFORE the click.
viz_units.encoding: Checkbox + label + right-aligned count that updates as other facets change; a value that would yield zero results is disabled rather than removed.
viz_units.data_source: computed client-side over clusters_index.json / search_index.json.gz
interactions: multi-select within a facet, AND across facets
state in the URL

viz_units.name: Range-slider facet with distribution backdrop
viz_units.what_it_shows: A numeric facet (cluster size 218-5,755; median position 0-1; partner count 0-62) with the population histogram drawn behind the track.
viz_units.encoding: Dual-handle slider over a 40px histogram; the selected range is highlighted in the histogram.
viz_units.data_source: clusters_index.json numeric fields
interactions: drag either handle; type exact bounds

viz_units.name: Sort control with an excluded-key note
viz_units.what_it_shows: The sort keys, and a visible note that npmi_raw is deliberately not among them.
viz_units.encoding: A select plus a small ⓘ that expands to 'raw NPMI is not offered as a sort key: 25 of its top 30 pairs are ZNF clade artifacts. See why we corrected for paralogy.'
viz_units.data_source: static copy bound to RAW_top30_annotated.csv's verdict counts
interactions: the ⓘ links to V13

viz_units.name: miRNA family row
viz_units.what_it_shows: One of the 219 TargetScan families with its motif count and the clusters where it is enriched.
viz_units.encoding: Family string (often long, e.g. 'miR-15-5p/16-5p/195-5p/424-5p/497-5p') with a wrap-safe layout, a count bar, and cluster chips.
viz_units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet column mirna_annotations_targetscan (219 distinct families, 24,228 utr3 motifs = 4.698%, 23 utr5) + cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz source=='miR' (15,798 rows, 22 clusters significant)
interactions: click -> the family's clusters and genes
link out to TargetScan by family name
viz_units.note: No miRBase accession mapping exists anywhere in the data, so deep links must be by family name and gene symbol, which is what TargetScan itself keys on.

viz_units.name: Term search row
viz_units.what_it_shows: One of the 15,979 distinct enrichment terms, its source, and how many clusters it is significant in.
viz_units.encoding: Term + source chip + a small bar of cluster count; InterPro terms carry their IPR accession.
viz_units.data_source: cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz grouped by (source, term); distinct terms per source InterPro 15,216, miR 219, ELM 156, eCLIP 150, IDPO 97, MobiDB 87, PAR-CLIP 57, iCLIP-P 32, iCLIP-C 22, SignalP 2
interactions: click -> the clusters where this term is significant, ranked by fold

viz_units.name: Sub-threshold partner table (greyed)
viz_units.what_it_shows: For the 282 UTR and 99 protein clusters with no strict partner, their best FAILING partners with the reason each failed.
viz_units.encoding: The same table as VU-C2-20 but rendered entirely in a muted style, with a per-row 'failed on:' column naming which of the four conditions was not met.
viz_units.data_source: protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv (all 180,000 pairs are present, so every one of the 900 clusters has rows) filtered to passes_phylo_filter==False and sorted by npmi_mip_APC
interactions: sort
click -> the edge drawer, which renders identically for failing pairs with red gate marks
viz_units.note: Showing the evidence landscape rather than only the curated subset is what stops a reader searching their favourite gene from concluding the site is hiding things.
